properties.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) near the UCSF Medical Center campus. The owner reviewed the numbered fragment map and picked fragment 49 as P26's real extent, then directed a further cut: the fragment forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide) -- keep the base, drop both forks.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20: the owner corrected the prior resolution (which had P26 'absorbed into the hospital's own footprint, not a separate parcel') using the numbered real-gap-fragment technique. Fragment 49 (a landscaped wedge between the I-280 ramps/curve near 16th St, 3rd St and Owens St, 4,384 sqm raw) forks above a widening base into two thin parallel strips flanking a walkway toward the UCSF building courtyard to the north -- found via a width-cross-section scan (nseg=2 for a wide latitude band, meaning two separate boundary crossings = two parallel arms) rather than eyeballed. Cut at the fork (lat 37.76495, where the cross-section width drops from a single 46m span to two separate ~17m arms) and kept only the single-segment base south of it, per the owner's 'keep the head, drop the horns' instruction. Result: 2,037 sqm triangular landscaped wedge in the freeway-ramp interchange.
